# Typed controller Points to scalar compressor PCM

Status: numbered #532 on delivered main `f39c9fa74016d4c0d460778a9c787668cbeb1e70` after #530 / PR #531 delivery. Root adopts the combined typed-controller/scalar constructor and its explicit trusted-binding/caller-clock limitations. This numbered issue awaits Astra current-base scope approval before implementation. Parent #140/#444 and audit #349 IO5 remain incomplete. Workflow: Astra briefs/reviews, Luna attempt1, Sol attempts2/3; root owns Git/GitHub and frequent exact-path checkpoints.

## One outcome

Add one opt-in host-core constructor that returns #530's actual typed controller and #528's scalar render owner sharing one delivery service. Real typed AutomationEnqueue -> controller validation/replay -> owned render claim -> scalar compressor PCM and native snapshot is the closable outcome. No standalone adoption prerequisite, second accepted-work copy, graph binding, framed/CAPI ingress, automatic host scheduling or live ParameterStateGet is included.

## Constructor and ownership

Use the existing control-provider feature and existing dependencies. Add `prepare_controller_scalar_point_endpoint<'a, P: protocol::ControlProvider>` taking, in order: `processor: &'a mut dyn PreparedNativeEffect`, `handles: [ParameterHandle;2]`, followed by the exact #530 preparation inputs `session: protocol::SessionStore`, `queues: ProtocolQueueConfig`, `provider: P`, `replay: ReplayCacheConfig`, `codec: ProtocolCodec`, `config: ProtocolControllerConfig`, `retained: ControllerRetainedCapacity`. No caller-supplied capabilities, revision or initial sequence: derive fixed revision from session and exact Point capabilities from the two handles; controller sequence starts1.

Return `(ControllerAutomationDelivery<P>, PreparedScalarPointRender<'a>, ControllerScalarPointResources)` or `ControllerScalarPointPrepareError`. Compact errors preserve existing `ScalarPointPrepareError` for native/handle/quantum rejection, typed `ParameterProviderError` for descriptor lookup, one `InvalidProviderBinding` mismatch case, `InitialSampleMismatch { observed: SampleTime }`, and `ControllerAutomationPrepareError` for fresh controller preparation. No boxed/string errors. No arbitrary externally populated render-half input or public unchecked adoption escape.

Factor #528's existing processor/binding validation and inline render assembly into private helpers. Existing standalone prepare_scalar_point_endpoint continues to create its standalone control/delivery pair and keeps its public behavior/report unchanged. The new constructor calls accepted #530 prepare once and directly moves its returned AutomationDeliveryRender into the shared inline assembler. No second PreparedAutomationDelivery::prepare call, re-admission or batch forwarding is allowed. Runtime render/snapshot/fault/cancel algorithms are unchanged.

## Frozen preflight

Perform all rejection-capable preflight before fresh controller preparation. Reuse exact existing native checks: strictly increasing nonzero handles, representable matching quantum, launch rate, Normal enabled dual-mono miso.compressor, optional unconnected sidechain, native index5/ID6 readable+automatable per-lane continuous dB[-24,24], linear64 smoothing, and FP-guarded Left/Right state reads. Do not silently broaden these checks.

Use `ControlProvider::parameter_descriptor` for each actual handle. Require descriptor.handle matches the requested handle; parameter_id6; respective protocol Left/Right channel; F32, Db, Continuous, min/max exactly -24/+24, default0, Linear mapping, Block automation rate, smoothing_samples64, readable/automatable/per-lane bits all set (`flags & 7 == 7`), no enum choices. Both descriptors must identify the same track_id/rack/effect_id instance. `effect_id` is the session instance ID, not the native factory ID; do not compare it to "miso.compressor". Check native factory identity through processor.metadata as above. Existing protocol descriptors have no smoothing-rule field: validate linear smoothing using native metadata, not an invented wire field. Block metadata does not prohibit the already approved #528 Point slicing capability.

The supplied session/provider and processor-to-session-instance association remain trusted prepared caller inputs, as with #528/#530; semantic metadata checks do not prove pointer identity or reconstruct a session binding graph. The fixture below supplies the actual same prepared entry. A custom provider must keep descriptors stable throughout the facade lifetime. To compare both location keys through the trait's mutable descriptor borrow, temporary control-side copies of only the first location strings are permitted; no new provider trait/helper framework is needed. These temporary allocations are excluded from retained reporting and must not be claimed allocation-free preparation. Reject provider.current_sample != SampleTime(0), since the reused render owner starts at zero; return `InitialSampleMismatch { observed }`.

After preflight, invoke #530 prepare and assemble the inline renderer infallibly. Failure publishes no halves or admissions; owned provider/session/preparation allocations drop off render and the caller retains its compressor. Do not promise rollback of arbitrary caller-provider side effects or universally recoverable OOM. Successful start failure returns the complete prepared render owner under #528's contract. After publication, accepted work requires real cancellation acknowledgment/quiescence before off-render reclamation; no drop-to-retry path.

`ControllerScalarPointResources` has `controller: ControllerAutomationResources` and `scalar_render_inline_bytes: usize`. Controller report retains all #530 exclusions. The scalar size is size_of<PreparedScalarPointRender>; it includes the embedded delivery render half, so it replaces controller.render_inline_bytes in any aggregate, never adds both. Borrowed processor, caller PCM, caller/session/provider storage and transient preflight copies are excluded. No whole-process peak claim or second delivery resource report.

## Real catalog/clock fixture

Use existing `fixtures/session/v1/compressor-dynamic-observation.json` (one compressor entry), existing session compile/prepare_native_session_effects, and `SessionControlProvider::prepare_session(&effects.entries)` followed by `SessionControlProvider::try_new`. Reuse the control_provider.rs fixture's minimal `Clock(AtomicU64)` implementing existing `PlanSampleSource`; no parallel ControlProvider mock subsystem. Build protocol SessionStore from the same model and borrow `effects.entries[0].processor.as_mut()` after preparing its real catalog. Resolve the actual Left/Right ID6 handles from provider metadata, not guessed constants; retain the same catalog instance location. Use the fixture's actual supported quantum/rate or one explicitly amended typed model value shared by all preparation, not a second inconsistent config.

The caller owns synchronization: initialize clock0, advance it to the endpoint's actual next_sample only after a successful render/between-block observation or cancellation-only boundary, before subsequent controller admission. Read snapshot does not itself publish a provider clock. A sticky-fault first envelope advances once as #528 already specifies; later fault returns do not invent progress. The fixture must exercise subsequent past-time rejection using the published nonzero sample. Automatic concurrent host clock publication remains out of scope; do not claim a permanently-zero mock as end-to-end timing evidence. Protocol ParameterStateGet stays Unavailable; actual native readback is endpoint.snapshot only.

## Three finite integration claim groups

1. Actual typed admission and decoded response, exact replay and retained ticket drive asymmetric real Left/Right PCM with one interior and one future/block-end Point. Compare with the existing #528 independent span-based native comparator (real current/target and existing payload oracle where useful); show replay does not apply twice. Publish actual next_sample into the existing clock and reject a subsequent past request without new ownership. Assert protocol StateGet remains Unavailable while native snapshot reflects the actual target/current.
2. A real two-record partial application (prefix1, not0), controller cancellation, actual endpoint boundary and the sole encoded event stream agree on applied1/canceled1, effective sample, native state and released credit. Reuse existing #528 fault-only cancellation proof on unchanged code; no new fault wrapper or matrix. No batch is copied into another service to drive this test.
3. Representative incompatible native processor and provider binding/clock failures publish no owner and leave the caller's processor usable; successful preparation shows one controller queue/delivery allocation authority by source composition and comparison against direct #530 preparation, accounting separately for explicitly allowed transient preflight allocations. Reuse existing counters/tooling and report proofs, not a new allocator/harness. Reused #528 positive/zero render evidence must still apply to the unchanged shared renderer.

Allowed paths: host-core/src/scalar_point_endpoint.rs, existing lib.rs exports, existing scalar endpoint test file or one small integration fixture. No provider production changes, protocol algorithm changes, new dependencies, effect algorithm, graph, browser or CAPI edits. Focused debug/release, host-core feature/default regressions, reused #530/#460 ownership checks, affected lint/doc/fmt/policies and scalar/SIMD compilation are proportional; immutable delivery remains native ABI/ordinary artifact identity and affected consumers/required CI/current-base review. No benchmark or broad new fixture matrix.

Half-day feasibility: one shared private validation/assembly extraction, one combined constructor and three real integration claims using existing catalog/PCM fixtures. No concrete prerequisite blocker is identified. If accepted #530 API changes before delivery, recheck its tuple/ownership seam at numbering. If real session/provider integration requires a live state overlay, graph identity resolver or automatic scheduler, stop and split that independent outcome; none is needed to prove this caller-owned typed request-to-PCM leaf.
